newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai white sugar lifting active in week, raws dull.
newsitem.headline: Thai white sugar lifting active in week, raws dull.

text.p: The Thai white sugar market was active with plenty of lifting going on while raw sugar premiums were depressed by lack of major purchases, trade sources said on Friday.
Traders said some mills were using up their local white quota to fulfil export obligations and would remelt the raw sugar to produce white at the end of the season to make up for the used amount.
There were 23 new declarations over the week for the lifting of 228,800 tonnes of sugar, mostly white. The major destination continued to be Indonesia, followed by Iran and Pakistan.
Thai white premium for 100 ICUMSA was offered without a bid at around US$27-30 per tonne over London for April/May delivery compared with $25 last week.
The raw premiums for May/July delivery edged down to 0.20/0.35 cents per pound (bid/offer) on FOB basis over New York futures from 0.25/0.40 cents a week earlier.

"The main activity in the white sugar market at present was basically loading. But there was not much fresh buying recently. I would expect the price to be steady near-term," said a trader from a major U.S. firm.

Traders said mills were running out of space for raw sugar stockpile due to sluggish trade and partly to holdbacks by millers who anticipated improved premiums later this year when major buyers China or the Philippines jumped into the market with major orders.

"Most of the nearby shipments had been sent out. The warehouses are full because there were only a small number of vessels coming in for raw sugar loading," said another trader from a major Japanese house.
"Moreover, many expect prices to improve later, so they hold back. But I don't know how long they can hold on to their stocks. There is almost no space left," he added.

On the supply side, crushing was reaching its peak with the yield improving constantly. As of March 17, Thai mills produced 4.94 million tonnes of sugar, 2.86 million tonnes of which were raw, according to industry sources.
The yield rose to 102.19 kg of sugar per tonne of cane from 100.98 kg during previous week.
Traders said the recent suspension of raw sugar production of two mills carried limited impact on the market as the mills did not produce a significant amount of raw sugar.
The two eastern mills were suspended because they produced raw sugar without licences. Both mills were allowed to produced brown sugar only.
